beats.care: If you ride the Pune–Nashik highway to Chakan or Bhosari daily, your wait at these two junctions could change soon.
beats.what: PCMC will fit an adaptive, AI-based signal system at Moshi Gaothan and Bharatmata junctions, then trial it for seven days.
beats.why: The city has listed 26 jam hotspots, and these signals change timing based on actual traffic instead of a fixed clock.

cards.body: They include Nashik Phata, Bhujbal Chowk, Dange Chowk and Dapodi Metro station.
cards.caption: Jam hotspots listed by PCMC

opts: It changes green time based on live traffic
cards.q: What makes an 'adaptive' traffic signal different?
cards.why: Adaptive systems adjust signal timing to the traffic actually waiting, not a fixed timer.

cards.body: PCMC has 154 signal-controlled junctions, but only two are getting the AI trial first.

hook: Can *a smart signal* finally fix the Moshi jam on your commute?

learn.t: Pimpri-Chinchwad has over 30 lakh registered vehicles, roughly one for every resident.

sources.name: Punekar News
sources.title: Pune: PCMC to Test AI-Powered Traffic Signals at Two Moshi Junctions

tldr: PCMC will try AI-powered traffic signals at two Moshi junctions on the Pune–Nashik highway.
watch: PCMC says the system will be installed within 15 days, followed by a seven-day trial.
